draft: In smoggy Mexico City, infrastructure struggles under constant construction funded by global financiers while residents ration trucked-in water due to insufficient rainstorms. Conflicts over water rights and corporate expansion lead to occasional protests. However, there is also an undercurrent of cooperation among neighbors adapting to changing circumstances through small garden plots, canal-irrigated runoff, mutual aid networks distributing produce and offering shelter during floods or heatwaves. Life goes on in a city navigating between cooperation and conflict, resilience and collapse.
